items.stem: An IT auditor notes that a change-management control 'exists' because a written procedure is on file. To conclude it is effective, the auditor should:

options.text: Test whether changes actually followed the procedure during the period
options.rationale: Correct: operating effectiveness requires testing real changes, not just a written procedure.

options.text: Accept the procedure document as sufficient
options.rationale: A document alone does not prove the control operates.

options.text: Ask the developer if it works
options.rationale: An informal assurance is not audit evidence.
Skipping testing leaves the conclusion unsupported.

items.explanation: Correct: operating effectiveness requires testing real changes, not just a written procedure.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which is an example of an IT general control rather than an application control?

options.rationale: Correct: access administration is an IT general control supporting many applications.

options.text: A field edit check on an invoice amount
options.rationale: A field edit check is an application control.

options.text: A duplicate-invoice check in one app
options.rationale: This is an application control within a single app.

options.text: A total-reconciliation routine in one module

items.explanation: Correct: access administration is an IT general control supporting many applications.

items.stem: An IT audit finding states 'access reviews are frequently late.' Which TWO additions make it a complete, useful finding? (Select TWO)

options.text: The risk or impact of the late reviews
options.rationale: Correct: stating risk shows why the finding matters.

options.text: The root cause of the lateness
options.rationale: Correct: root cause enables effective remediation.

options.text: The auditor's opinion of the staff's attitude
options.rationale: Personal opinions are inappropriate in findings.

options.text: A decision to omit the finding

items.explanation: Correct: stating risk shows why the finding matters. Correct: root cause enables effective remediation.
